children: The global economy could soon test the limits of resilience, says Silvana Tenreyro, chief economist at the IMF. Dwindling energy inventories could cause geopolitical shocks to be transmitted more forcefully to prices, while other commodity markets face risks from weather events and disruptions. The tech-related investment that is buffered against the energy shock has made growth reliant on select economies and sectors, she adds. Borrowing costs are climbing, public debt is high and fiscal buffers depleted. In a scenario where higher commodity prices and fiscal concerns spur reassessment of borrowing risks, global growth in 2027 could be much slower and inflation higher. "Keeping public debt on a durably sustainable path can prevent such a scenario."(fabiana.negrinochoa@wsj.com)
